manifest.cross_validation: see formal/results/reports/dyn_crossvalidation.json; the tracer engine is the one validated there

input_models.advance: closed-loop: holds RIGHT+B, jumps when the player's x position has not advanced for eight frames, crouches at random to find pipes; reads $0770, $006D and $0086
input_models.explore: run, plus random DOWN/UP/LEFT/START/SELECT at a few per cent
input_models.menu: START for three frames out of every 64
input_models.mixed: 600-frame blocks cycling the advance policy, explore, random and menu
input_models.random: uniformly random bytes, including LEFT+RIGHT and UP+DOWN together, which a standard pad cannot produce
input_models.replay:11: replayed controller bytes from /home/sadovsky/big/smb1-formal/replays/replay_11.json (16004 frames, 8 deaths, best world 1-2), then the closed-loop advance policy
input_models.replay:4: replayed controller bytes from /home/sadovsky/big/smb1-formal/replays/replay_4.json (16012 frames, 9 deaths, best world 1-3), then the closed-loop advance policy
input_models.title: no button is ever pressed (title screen and attract demo)

reading: at_nmi_entry[cell] is the set of values the cell held at an NMI entry, i.e. at a frame boundary with the handler about to run. ever_written[cell] is the set of values any instruction wrote into it. A value is written as an integer, a run as [lo, hi]. A cell absent from a map was never observed in that role.
